contracts.summary: The cutover contract is frozen by the rules below. It makes the singular demo chat, durable Stop, exact message mutations, real-source subscriptions, dormant publisher composition, empty live visualization, active database-backed sessions, replay-safe identity reset, strict citations, reference-default design system, and full deletion of the old product-chat and fixture paths mandatory. RESOLUTION entries settle every stale canonical claim, including the /docs conflict. No repository file was edited and no test or service was run.
contracts.frozenContractsArtifact: This JSON response is the authoritative cutover contract. It supersedes conflicting pre-cutover documentation and the earlier integration audit until P9 updates the canonical documents. No repository artifact was created because this task is read-only.
behaviorRules: AUTHORITY-001: Apply authority in this order: this frozen contract, settled decisions in artifacts/ui-playground-demo-implementation-plan.html, canonical docs after P9 sync, then current code and older reports as historical evidence only. A worker must stop if an implementation choice conflicts with a higher-ranked source.

RESOLUTION-001: Resolve the /docs conflict in favor of the cutover API. Keep the /docs route, packages/docs/src/html.ts, DOCS_HTML, deny-by-default CSP, required font grants, English lang attribute, and standalone UI-owned styling. Change every body section, heading, field, example, and link that describes a deleted /v1/chats route, explicit chat ID, done/error-only SSE, missing Stop, or another stale contract. Unaffected content remains unchanged. The post-P9 DOCS_HTML snapshot, not its pre-cutover bytes, becomes exact.

RESOLUTION-002: In docs/design.spec.md, replace two demo accounts, routable publisher views, fixture or IndexedDB documents, multi-chat sharing/archive/deletion, and archive-and-replace reset with one reachable client product, an unreachable publisher composition, real sources, one chat, and identity reset.

RESOLUTION-003: In docs/design-system.md, replace the Pressroom OKLCH and 0.5px-radius defaults with the complete tracked ui-playground hex-token and 2px-radius defaults. packages/ui is the sole shipped owner.

RESOLUTION-004: In docs/engineering.spec.md, remove publisher-fixture, explicit-chat-ID, chat-collection, and reset-chat requirements. Retain its strict-schema, migration, security, transaction, and Effect v4 rules.

RESOLUTION-005: In docs/ai-chat-runtime.spec.md, replace multiple-chat and no-Stop claims with the singular-chat and durable-Stop contract. Delete the legacy citation allowance. Retain durable SSE, provider, source, memory, access, and failure rules where they do not conflict.

RESOLUTION-006: In docs/data-access.spec.md, remove chat sharing, archive, chat deletion, archive reset, and legacy web-quote decoding. Retain derived-row, secure-document, memory, retention, and authorization rules where this contract keeps those features.

RESOLUTION-007: Keep docs/localization.spec.md ownership of schema-checked fr-FR.json and en-US.json catalogs. Locale and market pairing cannot restore a publisher route, fixture source, legacy translator, or alternate catalog.

RESOLUTION-008: Treat docs/expansion.spec.md publisher and market material as future context only. It cannot create a production publisher path, account switcher, command, link, navigation item, or chunk.

RESOLUTION-009: In docs/public-source-marketplace.research.md, retain support for real official sources, authenticated content, and source enablement. Remove invitation, fake-source, seeded-publication, and Read/Unread product claims.

RESOLUTION-010: The earlier artifacts/ui-playground-demo-integration-audit.html is background evidence only. Its publisher omission, empty-only visualization omission, unsupported Stop, archive/new-chat reset, and restored publisher fixtures do not apply.

RESOLUTION-011: Existing tests, route registries, migrations, or exports that prove the old product do not preserve that product. Tests and callers must change or disappear; migrations 0001 through 0073 remain only as immutable boot history.

ROUTE-001: The demo router may recognize only the pre-cutover client root, source, and publication route patterns. Unknown paths and every publisher or gallery path must select a branded not-found view. They must not redirect or normalize to the client root.

ROUTE-002: Production routing, navigation, command search, links, switchers, and lazy-import maps must contain no publisher or gallery destination. Direct dormant rendering is allowed only from a test or visual-fixture entry that the production entry graph cannot reach.

UI-001: packages/ui owns all shipped tokens, primitives, overlays, tables, chat presentation, visualization presentation, publisher presentation, and reusable states. apps/demo owns routes, controllers, fetches, SSE, locale and route state, command actions, and browser storage.

UI-002: Port the complete publisher composition with honest empty inputs. Keep it buildable and directly testable, but expose no product URL, router import, navigation item, switcher, command, palette result, or production chunk that can reach it.

UI-003: Port the complete visualization presentation, version controls, sandbox canvas, and message association. Reachable demo data must always contain zero real versions. The empty state must make version-dependent actions unavailable and must issue no visualization network request.

UI-004: Test-only publisher and visualization fixtures may render non-empty states for parity checks, but they must use static fixture data, remain outside the production dependency graph, and create no service mock, backend route, persistence contract, or fallback.

CHAT-001: The complete public chat route set is GET /v1/chat, POST /v1/chat/messages, GET /v1/ai-runs/:runId/stream, GET /v1/ai-runs/:runId/debug, POST /v1/ai-runs/:runId/stop, DELETE /v1/chat/messages/:messageId, and PATCH /v1/chat/messages/:messageId. No other /v1/chat or /v1/chats capability may ship.

CHAT-002: GET /v1/chat resolves the sole chat through the active demo session. The public response and request path contain no chatId. The database may keep one internal chat UUID for joins, locks, runs, and purge order.

CHAT-003: POST /v1/chat/messages accepts a strict JSON object with non-empty content and the required boolean webSearchEnabled. It rejects chatId and unknown fields, creates one user message and one queued run in one transaction, and returns 202 with the canonical queued-run projection.

CHAT-004: Public run status is exactly queued, running, succeeded, failed, or stopped. Debug projections use the same set. SSE has exactly one terminal event: done for succeeded, error for failed, or stopped for stopped.

STOP-001: POST /v1/ai-runs/:runId/stop accepts no request body. It requires an active session and a run owned by that session's internal chat. A missing or foreign run returns 404 rather than revealing ownership.

STOP-002: The first stop request for a queued or running run durably records stop intent and returns 202. A repeat while cancellation is pending returns the same accepted projection. A request for an already terminal run returns 200 with its unchanged terminal projection.

STOP-003: If stop wins, the worker cancels provider work, commits the generated text prefix and only citations that pass the strict citation schema, emits one stopped terminal event, exposes stopped through reload and debug, and creates no memory or later derived work. If zero text was generated, it creates no empty visible assistant row.

STOP-004: Completion and stop use one database compare-and-set boundary. A committed succeeded or failed result wins over a later stop. A committed stop fences later provider chunks, finalizers, memories, and terminal events. No run may have two terminal states or terminal SSE events.

STOP-005: SSE reconnection must replay the durable stopped terminal event with the existing durable event-ID rules. It must never synthesize done after stopped or depend on an in-memory cancellation flag for final truth.

CITATION-001: PublicCitationRecord has one strict canonical representation. Delete LegacyCitationRecord and every omitted-field, string-quote, coercion, alternate decoder, repair, and fallback branch. Invalid provider citation data fails through the canonical typed failure path.

MESSAGE-001: DELETE /v1/chat/messages/:messageId accepts no body. For an owned visible message it returns 204 and hides only that selected projection row. Its paired user or assistant row remains visible, and all raw events, runs, observations, source exposures, source uses, usage, citations, memories, and revisions remain stored.
MESSAGE-002: DELETE returns 404 for a missing, foreign, or already hidden message. It must not invoke delete-chat behavior, cascade through the pair, rewrite history, or remove derived rows.

MESSAGE-003: PATCH /v1/chat/messages/:messageId accepts only a strict JSON object containing non-empty content. It applies only when the target is the last visible user question; a missing or foreign target returns 404, and an assistant or non-last visible user message returns 409.

MESSAGE-004: A successful PATCH keeps the question's public message identity, records the new question revision, excludes the prior run from the current projection, hides its old visible answer if present, retains all prior raw and derived rows, and creates exactly one replacement queued run in the same locked transaction. It returns 202 with the canonical queued-run projection.

MESSAGE-005: An active old run superseded by PATCH must receive a durable write fence and cancellation signal. It cannot append text, citations, memories, or a terminal event to the current projection after the edit. Supersession does not add a compatibility route or a second public run-status vocabulary.
FEATURE-001: Ship no Regenerate action, attachment picker, attachment request field, attachment storage, attachment route, hidden attachment trigger, or related dependency.
FEATURE-002: Keep browser dictation. It may only place transcript text into the composer and must not create a second send path or upload audio.

FEATURE-003: Show suggestions only after a successful run when visible chat history is empty. Suggestions must come from the locale catalogs and must not appear during queued, running, failed, or stopped states.

WEB-001: Persist webSearchEnabled through the one browser-storage registry and default it to true when no valid stored value exists. The send schema must validate it. The server's EffectiveWebPolicy remains final and may deny web use despite the client preference; no client fallback may bypass it.

SOURCE-001: Subscription screens list only real public-source rows that the active identity may access. A row with subscribed false remains visible and shows its disabled state. Source publications do not disappear merely because the source is disabled.

SOURCE-002: Each source toggle has its own pending state. The UI may update that row optimistically, but on failure it restores the prior value and shows a localized visible error. A per-row request generation or equivalent token must prevent an older response from overwriting newer route, session, or mutation state.
SOURCE-003: Keep the real source-list, toggle, and secure-document paths. Remove invitations, seeded issues, fixture PDFs, fake account or plan metrics, and Read/Unread state.

SESSION-001: Every demo-product request except explicit session bootstrap and reset replay must resolve the cookie to an existing active database session. A cookie-safe slug, unknown ID, revoked session, or client-created value does not authenticate and receives 401.

SESSION-002: The explicit bootstrap operation is the only path that may create a fresh active session for a request with no session cookie. It creates the row before accepting product work. It must not silently replace an unknown or revoked cookie.

RESET-001: POST /v1/demo/session/reset is the only reset endpoint. It accepts a strict body containing one UUID operationId, requires the current session or the narrow replay exception, and returns 202 with a successor-session cookie and the durable reset-operation projection before purge completes.

RESET-002: Under one database lock and transaction, the first reset operation creates exactly one successor session, records the operation and purge job outside the old identity graph, and revokes the old session before the 202 response. A replay with the same operationId returns the same successor. A different operationId for the same old session returns 409 and creates nothing.

RESET-003: The reset endpoint may recognize a revoked old session only to replay its already recorded operationId. That exception cannot authorize chat, source, memory, document, stream, debug, or mutation requests.
RESET-004: Reset exists only as a localized confirmed command-palette action. No header icon, route button, account switcher, hidden shortcut, archive action, or new-chat action may call it.

RESET-005: After a successful 202, the client closes streams, runs the sole registered-storage clearer, clears in-memory query, chat, locale-dependent, and mutation state, installs the successor cookie through the response, and performs a hard reload. Bootstrap must recover a durable pending reset if the response or reload was interrupted.

RESET-006: Revocation and session-generation checks fence all late writes, stream chunks, source toggles, message mutations, memories, exports, and job results associated with the old identity. Client-side clearing alone is never the security boundary.

RESET-007: The purge job is restart-safe and has no maximum total row cap. It may use bounded batches, but it must continue until every row in the old identity graph is gone, retain global public-source catalog data, and never traverse into the successor session.

I18N-001: Every shipped or dormant label, aria string, count, error, suggestion, reset confirmation, publisher fixture, and visualization fixture must be keyed in both schema-checked fr-FR.json and en-US.json catalogs. Inline user-facing literals and the ui-playground translator cannot ship.

DESIGN-001: packages/ui must use the complete tracked ui-playground token set as its sole default: the reference hex values, 2px radius, typography, spacing, component states, overlays, tables, chat, publisher controls, and visualization parts. The prior active OKLCH palette and 0.5px default must not remain as an alternate theme or fallback.

ACCESS-001: All reachable and direct dormant fixtures must support keyboard-only operation, visible focus, correct accessible names, valid dialog focus management, and reduced-motion behavior. Disabled visualization controls must remain discoverable but cannot dispatch an action.
dependencyBoundaries: DEP-001: ui-playground remains outside the root apps/* and packages/* workspaces and keeps its own package-lock.json. No root workspace manifest may add it.

DEP-002: No production source, test helper used by production, package manifest, TypeScript path alias, Vite alias, CSS import, asset URL, copy task, code-generation task, dynamic import, or runtime file read may reference ui-playground. Ported code becomes owned packages/ui code with no sync or fallback path.

DEP-003: The production build graph for apps/demo must reach packages/ui but must not reach a publisher entry, gallery entry, ui-playground, @hartlib/demo-data, or @hartlib/backend-domain/product-chats.
DEP-004: packages/ui may depend on React-facing UI libraries but cannot fetch product data, open SSE, read demo routes, read product browser storage, call API clients, or import from apps/demo.

DEP-005: apps/demo owns route and locale state, commands, fetch and SSE controllers, web-search preference, reset orchestration, and browser storage. It cannot own reusable design-system primitives or duplicate shared HTTP codecs.

DEP-006: Shared request, response, SSE, run-status, citation, session, reset, and message-mutation codecs have one owner under packages/shared. API, worker, API client, demo, docs generation, and tests import those codecs rather than defining parallel shapes.
DEP-007: apps/api and its tests must not import @hartlib/backend-domain/product-chats. Remove the product-chats module and its barrel exports once all callers are removed.
DEP-008: apps/demo must not depend on @hartlib/demo-data. Delete that workspace package and all fake account, plan, issue, PDF, and publication consumers.

DEP-009: Backend code must not add a visualization route, visualization persistence model, fake generation service, or placeholder provider. Live visualization state remains an honest empty input to the UI.
DEP-010: Publisher and visualization parity fixtures may depend on packages/ui and locale catalogs only. They must remain test-only entry points and must not appear in a production bundle metafile.

DEP-011: Add only UI packages imported by the final owned port. This includes cmdk, react-resizable-panels, rehype-highlight, and the exact overlay primitives actually imported. Every direct import must have one declared dependency, and every newly declared dependency must have at least one final import.

DEP-012: New backend work must use Effect 4.0.0-beta.92 patterns from docs/references/effect-smol. It must not import the Smithers-only effect3 alias, use JavaScript try/catch around yielded effects, or add an older Effect compatibility layer.

DEP-013: Reusable Effect functions use Effect.fnUntraced, services use class-based Context.Service, terminal effects use return yield*, scoped work owns its resources, and time-sensitive tests use TestClock.
DEP-014: The two locale JSON catalogs remain the only product string source. No reference translator, third catalog, generated fallback catalog, or inline English fallback may enter the graph.
DEP-015: packages/docs keeps standalone UI-owned CSS and font declarations. It must not import the demo app, packages/ui runtime components, or ui-playground to render /docs.

DEP-016: One browser-storage registry owns every demo key and its clearer. Feature modules may register typed entries but may not call localStorage.clear, indexedDB.deleteDatabase, or maintain a second reset list.

DEP-017: apps/web has no blanket retention. P1 must assign every retained apps/web file or export to a named required-infrastructure use. Explicit-chat, publisher, client, platform, or support code with no named retained caller must be deleted.

DEP-018: Deterministic providers may remain only where already required for isolated regression tests. They cannot prove live behavior, ship in the demo runtime, back a fallback route, or substitute for a requested real-provider gate. Add no new mock.

migrationRules: MIG-001: Add exactly one immutable migration with basename 0074_demo_product_cutover.sql in the existing migration directory. The loader must find it through the normal Effect Migrator path; no manual startup SQL may duplicate it.
MIG-002: Verify SHA-256 hashes for every migration 0001 through 0073 before and after implementation. The known missing 0065 number remains a valid historical gap and must not be filled.

MIG-003: Migration 0074 performs a hard cutover. It may drop and recreate affected live tables, types, constraints, indexes, triggers, and projections and must delete old demo rows. It must not backfill old chat data or create a compatibility view, alias, repair function, dual schema, or legacy decoder.

MIG-004: The post-0074 live schema permits at most one internal chat row per active demo session through a database uniqueness constraint. No public collection, share, archive, replacement-chat lineage, or user-selectable chat identifier remains.

MIG-005: Create durable demo-session state with opaque server-generated IDs, active and revoked state, creation and revocation timestamps, and the data needed to fence writes. Authentication must query this state rather than validate cookie syntax.

MIG-006: Create durable reset-operation state keyed by operationId and old session, with a uniqueness rule that allows exactly one successor per old session. Store the successor link, operation status, attempt data, and timestamps outside the rows purged with the old identity.
MIG-007: Create or adapt a restart-safe purge job keyed to the reset operation. Its ownership and foreign keys must not cascade from the old session, user, company, membership, or chat.

MIG-008: Add message-projection state needed to hide one visible row without deleting its pair or derived rows, and revision or supersession state needed to edit the last visible user question while keeping prior evidence.

MIG-009: Add the stopped terminal run state to every durable run-status constraint or database type and add durable stop-intent and write-fence data. Public projection, debug, SSE, and worker queries must derive from the same stored state.

MIG-010: Enforce one terminal transition per run with database constraints and compare-and-set updates. succeeded, failed, and stopped are mutually exclusive and cannot receive later chunks or terminal events.
MIG-011: Preserve the current canonical citation storage shape only. Migration 0074 must not translate legacy citation rows because old demo rows are discarded.

MIG-012: Remove live share, archive, deleted-chat, replacement-chat lineage, collection-ordering, and explicit-chat objects where they exist. Their names may survive only inside immutable historical migration text.

MIG-013: Audit every foreign key and queued job reachable from the old identity. The purge must cover chat messages, runs, run events, observations, source exposures, source uses, usage, memories, memory revisions, subscription bindings, exports, identity-scoped documents, jobs, chats, memberships, companies, users, and the old session wherever those rows belong to that identity.
MIG-014: Retain global public-source catalog and publication rows. Purge only identity-owned enablement, access, chat, memory, usage, export, and session data.

MIG-015: Purge may process bounded batches but must persist its cursor and retry state and continue until no old-identity row remains. No constant may cap total rows, attempts, pages, or elapsed restarts in a way that leaves data behind.

MIG-016: Apply 0074 transactionally through Effect's PostgreSQL and Migrator APIs where PostgreSQL permits. Any non-transactional operation must have an explicit restart-safe guard and an integration test; a JavaScript catch-and-continue path is forbidden.

MIG-017: Test both a fresh database applying 0001 through 0074 and an upgrade database populated with representative pre-0074 multi-chat, archive, citation, source, memory, usage, job, and identity rows. Both paths must end at the same asserted schema and empty old demo graph.
MIG-018: Record 0074 once in the migration ledger with its real checksum. A second application must be a no-op through the migrator, not through custom existence fallbacks.
verificationGates: GATE-001: Before implementation, capture HEAD, branch, upstream, ahead/behind counts, staged diff, unstaged diff, untracked names, hashes of the 34 protected untracked files, and the upstream commit diff. The incomplete starting-worktree artifact alone cannot satisfy this gate.

GATE-002: Complete the P1 named-use audit before deleting mixed files. Produce one row per retained apps/web, API, shared, API-client, backend-domain, demo-data, packages/ui, and apps/demo export, naming its reachable-demo, dormant-fixture, or required-infrastructure caller. Any unlisted old-product export must be deleted.

GATE-003: Hash the exact git ls-files -z ui-playground set before and after work and require all 69 path/hash pairs to match baseline/ui-playground-manifest.json. Do not include ignored or generated files in either digest domain.
GATE-004: Require git diff --exit-code over every pre-0074 migration and require exactly one tracked file named 0074_demo_product_cutover.sql.

GATE-005: Run 0074 through the real Effect migrator against fresh and populated PostgreSQL databases. Assert tables, types, constraints, indexes, foreign keys, migration ledger, row removal, singular-chat uniqueness, session revocation, terminal-state exclusivity, and second-run idempotence by database queries rather than SQL text search.

GATE-006: Enumerate the API route registry and shared/client exports. Fail if any removed /v1/chats route, share, unshare, archive, delete-chat, reset-chat, list/create chat method, explicit-chat path, optional chatId, or compatibility alias remains.
GATE-007: Exercise strict request decoding. Unknown fields and chatId must fail for singular send and mutation requests; legacy citation forms must fail; canonical requests and citations must pass.

GATE-008: Build the full root workspace and apps/demo. Inspect dependency graphs and bundler metafiles and fail on ui-playground, @hartlib/demo-data, product-chats, publisher entry, gallery entry, reference translator, shipped mock, or test-fixture reachability.

GATE-009: Compare all new dependency declarations with final static and dynamic imports. Fail on undeclared direct imports, unused newly added dependencies, duplicate versions introduced without need, or changes to ui-playground/package-lock.json.

GATE-010: Run targeted unit tests for route parsing, branded not-found selection, strict schemas, run terminal transitions, stop idempotence, completion/stop races, message visibility, last-question edit validation, source visibility, stale-response fencing, storage registration, localization parity, and Effect TestClock behavior.

GATE-011: Run API, worker, and PostgreSQL integration tests for first stop, repeated stop, stop before provider start, stop during text, stop with citations, completion winning, failure winning, SSE reconnect after stopped, and rejection of foreign runs. Assert one durable terminal event and no memory after stopped.

GATE-012: Test DELETE on user and assistant rows. Assert only the selected row disappears after reload, its pair remains, every derived row count remains unchanged, and a repeated, missing, or foreign delete returns 404.

GATE-013: Test PATCH on the last visible user question. Assert a stable question identity, stored revision, hidden old answer, retained old derived rows, one replacement run, cancellation and fencing of any active old run, and 409 for assistant or non-last questions.

GATE-014: Test active-session authentication with no cookie, a valid active row, an arbitrary cookie-safe slug, an unknown ID, and a revoked ID. Only explicit bootstrap may create a session for the no-cookie case.

GATE-015: Test reset with concurrent identical requests, a replay after revocation, a different operationId, response loss, server restart, worker restart, old-cookie reads and writes, late stream chunks, and hard reload. Assert one successor, immediate revocation, stable replay, 409 for the competing operation, and no old-session write after revocation.

GATE-016: Populate every audited old-identity table with more rows than each purge batch size, run reset, restart the purge worker between batches, and require zero remaining old-graph rows with successor and global source rows intact. A small fixture below the former cap does not pass.

GATE-017: Test source lists with enabled and disabled authorized rows. Both must remain visible through reload. Test per-row pending state, rollback and localized error on failure, and a delayed stale response that cannot overwrite newer state.

GATE-018: Test webSearchEnabled with absent, valid true, valid false, and invalid stored data. Assert default true, schema-checked persistence through the one registry, inclusion in send requests, and server EffectiveWebPolicy authority.

GATE-019: Keep and run the exact live baseline with real credentials: HARTLIB_E2E_LIVE_PROVIDER=1 HARTLIB_E2E_STACK=1 bun --env-file=.env x --bun playwright test tests/e2e/chat.spec.ts --project=hartlib-ai-chat-runtime -g "real provider internal retrieval persists a cited answer".

GATE-020: Add and run flow-specific Playwright tests with the live stack and real provider for a stopped partial answer and last-question edit replacement. Each must exercise UI submission, API, worker, provider, durable database result, SSE, and reload. A deterministic provider cannot satisfy this gate.

GATE-021: Run full-stack Playwright reset, message-delete, source-toggle, docs, routing, and persistence flows with real credentials where a provider is involved. Every required test must report passed; skipped, flaky-retried-only, or missing-credential exits do not pass.

GATE-022: Allocate a free HARTLIB_E2E_PORT_BASE, pass it to every stack command, and run shared-state or shared-port full-stack suites serially with one worker. Do not run competing stack builds or Playwright suites in parallel.

GATE-023: Render the live client, /docs, branded 404, direct dormant publisher fixture, and direct visualization fixtures at every viewport declared by the tracked ui-playground visual generator. Compare them with the permanent reference using the same locale, data, fonts, and motion settings.

GATE-024: Record visual differences and approve only settled differences: no reachable publisher/gallery, real rather than mock data, honest empty live visualization, singular chat, new Stop/mutation/reset controls, and updated docs. Unlisted visual drift fails.

GATE-025: Verify the live visualization shows the complete presentation with zero versions, disabled version-dependent actions, correct message association, and no visualization network request. Verify direct fixtures cover populated, empty, loading, disabled, and error presentation states without entering a production chunk.

GATE-026: Run keyboard and automated accessibility checks on client, command palette and reset confirmation, source rows, chat actions, visualization, publisher fixture, docs, and 404. Fail on serious violations, missing accessible names, focus loss, inaccessible pending/error state, or reduced-motion violations.

GATE-027: Validate fr-FR.json and en-US.json against the catalog schema and require identical key sets. Scan shipped and dormant UI source for inline user-facing strings and any reference translator import.

GATE-028: Request /docs and assert 200, English lang, deny-by-default CSP, only required font grants, standalone styling, current singular routes, Stop, stopped SSE/debug state, message mutations, and absence of every /v1/chats or legacy-citation claim.

GATE-029: Request known client routes, malformed client routes, publisher paths, gallery paths, and arbitrary paths. Assert only the client allowlist resolves to client views and all others render the branded 404 without a client-root fallback.

GATE-030: Scan source, manifests, generated route lists, docs output, build output, and tests for removed endpoint strings, @hartlib/demo-data, product-chats, LegacyCitationRecord, localStorage.clear, IndexedDB PDF code, Regenerate, attachment contracts, invitation state, old reset, compatibility aliases, fallback paths, dual implementations, and added mocks. Any executable occurrence fails; immutable migration history may contain old SQL terms.

GATE-031: Run the repository's distinct formatting, lint, type-check, unit, integration, build, and E2E commands. Do not label two identical bun run test invocations as separate unit and integration proof.
GATE-032: Re-run all gates after P9 documentation sync and after the final production build. Final approval requires every mandatory gate to pass in that final tree.
evidenceRequirements: EVIDENCE-001: Store evidence under artifacts/implement-ui-playground-demo-cutover with a stable index that maps every AUTHORITY, RESOLUTION, behavior, dependency, retention, deletion, migration, and verification ID to one or more concrete artifacts.

EVIDENCE-002: For each command, record the exact command, working directory, UTC timestamp, exit code, duration, relevant tool versions, and untruncated stdout and stderr or their content-addressed artifact paths.

EVIDENCE-003: Record only credential variable names and whether each required value was present. Never read, print, hash, screenshot, or copy ZAI_API_KEY, cookies, bearer tokens, database passwords, or other secret values.

EVIDENCE-004: Preserve the fixed plan identity with its path, 438-line and 77040-byte inventory, and a content hash. Record the repository start HEAD fe405755b98c2c8170635282a1f0fea1013d2dd1, upstream 568e919c4b48d95ee24adeafc80a53e1c06e5529, and complete starting-state evidence.

EVIDENCE-005: Produce source-to-target and named-use manifests for every ported component and every retained mixed-file export. Each row must name the final owner, production reachability, direct-fixture reachability, locale ownership, and dependency reason.

EVIDENCE-006: Produce a deletion manifest listing each removed file, symbol, route, schema, dependency, test, doc claim, fixture, and caller. Pair it with negative scans of source, manifests, docs output, route output, and build output.

EVIDENCE-007: Produce a retention manifest for the 69 tracked ui-playground files, migrations 0001 through 0073, protected Smithers files, canonical docs, and unrelated starting commits. Use the same path and hash domain before and after each comparison.

EVIDENCE-008: Do not compare currentRepositoryDigest with a manifest-only digest or expect the whole repository digest to remain equal after implementation. Compare protected subsets for equality and record the implementation diff separately.

EVIDENCE-009: Produce dependency evidence from workspace manifests, lock data, import scans, TypeScript resolution, and production bundle metafiles. Compute reference and dormant dependency counts from actual graphs; do not hard-code zero.

EVIDENCE-010: Produce migration evidence containing pre-0074 hashes, migrator output, migration-ledger rows, fresh and upgrade schema dumps, constraint and index queries, representative pre-cutover seed counts, post-cutover counts, and second-run results.

EVIDENCE-011: Produce reset and purge evidence containing operation rows, session rows, job attempts and cursor changes, concurrency results, restart points, old-cookie HTTP results, fenced-write results, per-table before/after counts, and proof that the successor and global sources survived.

EVIDENCE-012: Produce Stop evidence containing HTTP responses, durable run and event rows, provider cancellation timing, partial text and canonical citations, memory counts, debug projections, SSE transcripts including reconnect, and completion-versus-stop race outcomes.

EVIDENCE-013: Produce message-mutation evidence containing pre/post visible projections, raw and derived row IDs and counts, replacement-run cardinality, revision data, reload results, and all 404 or 409 cases.

EVIDENCE-014: Produce source-toggle evidence containing authorized enabled and disabled list responses, browser states, request-generation values, delayed response order, rollback state, localized error output, and persisted reload state.

EVIDENCE-015: For every Playwright gate, retain the HTML report, machine-readable result, trace, screenshots, video when configured, server logs, API and worker logs, database identifiers, test title, project name, port base, and whether the live-provider flag was active.

EVIDENCE-016: A mandatory live test counts only when Playwright reports passed with HARTLIB_E2E_LIVE_PROVIDER=1, HARTLIB_E2E_STACK=1, real credentials, and the requested full-stack path. Skipped, deterministic-only, mocked, manually inferred, or zero-exit-with-skip evidence is invalid.

EVIDENCE-017: Produce visual evidence as matched reference and candidate images with viewport, locale, fixture, commit, font, and reduced-motion metadata, plus machine diff output and a reviewed list containing only the settled differences.

EVIDENCE-018: Produce accessibility evidence with tool output and manual keyboard results for focus order, focus restoration, names, status announcements, pending and error states, and reduced motion. Screenshots alone do not prove accessibility.
EVIDENCE-019: Produce localization evidence with schema results, key-set comparison, missing/extra key reports, and scans for inline labels and translator imports.

EVIDENCE-020: Produce /docs and routing evidence from real HTTP responses, headers, rendered DOM, extracted links, route-manifest output, and direct browser navigation to client, bad, publisher, and gallery paths.
EVIDENCE-021: Final testEvidence and visualEvidence arrays must be non-empty and enumerate every mandatory artifact. Missing artifacts fail the workflow even if a summary says tests passed.
EVIDENCE-022: Set zeroActionableWork from the measured final diff and deletion manifest. It cannot be true for this unimplemented cutover and must never be hard-coded to satisfy retention.
EVIDENCE-023: Treat the repository audit, preflight, and earlier report as inputs, not completion proof. Re-run every mutable check after implementation and after final docs sync.

EVIDENCE-024: Record final HEAD, conventional commit subjects, branch and upstream relation, staged and unstaged diffs, untracked paths, protected-file hashes, implementation diff, test results, and outstanding failures. Claim completion only when every mandatory gate passes and no required work remains.

waves.summary: Twenty-eight disjoint work items form nine ordered waves. Dedicated integration owners control all barrels, manifests, route registries, and lock data. The plan protects the reference tree and historical migrations, uses only static data in isolated visual fixtures, and requires real PostgreSQL, real services, live provider credentials, durable state, serial full-stack runs, and exact failure checks. No item uses a mock, placeholder, compatibility path, fallback, or best-effort proof.

wavePlan.purpose: Capture the complete start state, protected hashes, named-use allowlist, source-to-target map, dependency inventory, and exact mutation ownership before implementation.
Land the strict shared contracts, the sole 0074 migration, and the reference-default UI foundation as independent parallel work.
Create database-backed sessions and port the client chat, visualization, and dormant publisher presentation into package-owned UI lanes.
Cut over the singular chat, real sources, durable Stop and supersession, replay-safe reset and purge, package exports, API client, and exact route registry.
Wire one storage registry, session and reset control, chat control, real-source routing, complete catalogs, isolated parity fixtures, empty live visualization, and branded not-found behavior.
Delete every obsolete product-chat, fixture, publisher route, gallery, demo-data, old reset, platform UI, and unused dependency path after its replacement is integrated.
Author exact database, API, worker, UI, routing, storage, localization, bundle, and accessibility checks while P9 replaces every stale canonical claim and DOCS_HTML section.
Run the live-provider and real-stack Playwright flows serially on a free port range, including Stop, edit, delete, reset, sources, routing, docs, persistence, visuals, and accessibility.
Rebuild and rerun every gate after P9, compare protected subsets, inspect final graphs and bundles, and publish indexed test, visual, lifecycle, migration, and repository evidence.
